text:
Nico Hischier, the Devils' captain, is in a goal race on his own team. Mike Fink of The Hockey News noted that Jack Hughes and Arseny Gritsyuk share the team lead with eight, with Hischier right behind at seven. The same reporter also figures Sheldon Keefe wants to get Hischier's line going, and that's the odd part of his season: the center is scoring, the line around him isn't.

He has 10 points in 16 games, six on the power play, but only three assists. At 5v5 New Jersey gets 61% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and his teammates have scored 2.5 fewer goals than those chances deserve. That's a good line getting poor finishing from its wingers, not a bad line. It's an old story for him: Evolving-Hockey had him 96th percentile among forwards at driving play last season, with results well behind his chances. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds a signature, 20% of his setups coming from behind the net. When his wingers start converting, the assists will come in bunches.
headline: Hischier is scoring; his wingers aren't yet
